claims.text: Compliance means meeting rules set from outside, by a regulator or a large customer's contract, and being able to show it with evidence rather than only say so; compliance-controls.md defines it this way and says it is not legal advice.
Each requirement is met by a control (a specific practice or mechanism), and each control needs evidence someone else can inspect; the table records what is true at stage-4.

A bank-owned chain of shops (an assumption of the example) sends seven requirements TT-1 to TT-7 before signing: second reviewer, tracing actions on orders and refunds, invoice key in its device, restore tests, components and vulnerabilities, data location, access reviews.

TT-1's control: every production change is a commit to envs/production of the config repository and nobody edits the cluster by hand (NT4 of architecture-governance.md); evidence is that repository's Git history, made automatically.

In the lab one commit by scripts/devops/gitops-promote.sh is enough to move the api to production, so the author is also the approver; the plan is a required pull request approved by someone other than the author on the production config repository (H6 of technical-strategy.md).
gitops-promote.sh commits to envs/production with no review step; its comment says that at work this commit would be a pull request, so review and required checks decide when production changes.
claims.source_hint: scripts/devops/gitops-promote.sh @ stage-4, comment above staging_tag and config_commit

claims.text: Each ci.yml run that passes the tests writes and scans an SBOM per image; a High or Critical vulnerability with a fix fails the run unless .grype.yaml accepts it with a reason. Service images pushed from master are signed with provenance and SBOM attestations; fake-gateway is not.
claims.source_hint: .github/workflows/ci.yml @ stage-4 jobs image (needs: test), publish, publish-fake-gateway; docs/team/compliance-controls.md line 35

claims.text: TT-5 gap: SBOMs and scan results are kept only as long as the run's artifacts are retained; the plan stores the SBOM of each release that reached production with its deploy commit.

TT-2: the audit log of docs/design/audit-log.md is only a design, not built at stage-4, and requested_by of a refund row can be changed without trace; TT-7: nobody reviews Keycloak roles or config repository rights on a schedule. Both have plans.

Đơn Hàng's principles prefer evidence made by the pipeline on every change (SBOMs, scan results, signatures, Git history) over evidence gathered by hand before an audit, as cheaper and harder to fake.
The team's rule: a gap is written down with a plan, not hidden, because a gap the inspector finds first costs more trust than one the team stated itself.

TT-4: evidence is the output of restore-test.sh (row counts against the dump, restore time) and dr-drill.sh (time of each step); the scripts run by themselves but are started by hand, not on a schedule.

TT-4 gap: backups and WAL have not left the machine running the database (ADR 0020); the plan copies them to a second location (action H4 of technical-strategy.md), runs restore tests on a schedule and keeps each output as the record.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/compliance-controls.md @ stage-4 line 34, last column; docs/team/technical-strategy.md H4

claims.text: TT-6: ADR 0020 and ADR 0022 decided where Đơn Hàng runs (one region, a provider's managed Kubernetes); architecture-governance.md's table of assumptions to watch lists a contract requiring data in a stated place as a reopen condition of both; reopen them before signing.
TT-3: the invoice signing key sits in the provider's HSM service and only Payments' ServiceAccount may sign (ADR 0015, 0023); decided but not built at stage-4.

Trade-offs: pipeline-made evidence fits controls a machine already runs; hand-gathered evidence fits human acts like access reviews and lapses when forgotten; a bare statement fits no outside rule; a stated gap fits a control not built yet.

If TT-1 became a condition of signing, moving the TT-1 part of H6 forward (a required reviewer other than the author on production config changes) is a sensible answer; the table keeps stating the gap until then.
claims.source_hint: compliance-controls.md line 31; technical-strategy.md H6; roadmap.md 'Tiếp theo'

claims.text: The bank's inspector checks the controls for the requirements on the bank's list; a risk the threat model found can sit outside every listed rule, so passing the bank's audit does not prove the system secure.

Every control in the table is an engineering mechanism (a commit path, a CI step, an HSM, a restore script), so only engineers can say whether it runs; a filed document stops matching the system as soon as a control or a gap changes.
ADR 0015 keeps the invoice signing key in an HSM that only Payments may call.

beyond_scope: Try it and one choice use TT-4 and TT-6 rows of the quoted table; no restore-testing or ADR 0020/0022 content beyond what those rows say.
